summary: Captive-portal / TLS interception by corporate NGFW returns HTML login page for presigned S3 URLs, causing model artifact fetch failures in private deploy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent failures pulling model shard objects from S3 when running a Private deployment behind their corporate NGFW. Instead of binary object, the HTTP range request returns an HTML captive‑portal/login page (200 OK, text/html). This causes model shard validation to fail and the serving node to mark shards corrupted, producing 5xx errors for in-flight inference requests.

Impact:
- Production latency spikes and increased 5xx on a subset (~12%) of artifact range requests.
- Several serving nodes marked unhealthy and restarted model pulls, amplifying load.
- Customer experienced production degradation of one internal ML feature for ~2 hours during business peak.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC with VPCE to S3 disabled (customer downloads via egress NAT through corporate perimeter).
- Serving runtime version: rwd-infer-1.18.2
- Artifact store: s3://redwood-models-prod/fin/bert-large-serve-v2/
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy private package into customer VPC with default egress to corporate internet via NGFW
2) Trigger a model load (e.g., scale up serving nodes) to force range GETs for shard files
3) Observe repeated HTTP 200 responses with content-type text/html instead of application/octet-stream
4) Serving runtime logs show checksum mismatch and shard validation failure followed by retry loop
logs_and_artifacts: Sample HTTP transaction: GET /bert-large-serve-v2/weights/shard-3?X-Amz-Signature=... -> 200 OK, Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8, body starts with '<!DOCTYPE html>'
Serving node logs: runtime/artifact_fetch.cpp:line 214 checksum mismatch for shard-3, expected 0x1f4b2a got 0x000000
PCAP (customer-provided): tcpdump shows corporate NGFW injecting 302 -> captive.login.local:8080 for the GET request before TLS unwrap
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Patel: Customer first reported degradation in #support with screenshot of HTML body returned for shard range requests.
2026-03-10 10:02 - Diego Ramos (Support): Confirmed serving node logs show non-binary responses for range GETs; escalated to SRE for network evidence collection.

2026-03-10 13:40 - SRE (Anya Chen): Packet capture shows TLS is being intercepted/terminated by corporate NGFW which returns captive portal content for outbound HTTPS to S3 hosts that are not allowlisted. Customer policy notes show forced TLS inspection for unknown external hosts.

2026-03-11 08:22 - Customer (Network Ops, Aaron Li): Confirmed corporate NGFW performs HTTPS intercept and redirects unauthenticated devices to captive portal unless destination on exception list. They initially blocked allowlist changes for security review.

2026-03-12 11:05 - Diego Ramos: Proposed mitigations (1) configure VPCE to S3 or (2) request permanent allowlist for redwood-models-prod S3 hostnames and S3 IP ranges; asked customer to trial VPCE first.
2026-03-13 15:30 - Customer (Aaron Li): Started VPCE pilot and reported artifact pulls succeeded during test window; agreed to open change request with infosec to allowlist in long term.
investigation_notes: Observed pattern: only requests that traverse corporate perimeter are affected. When the same nodes egress via a jump server with no TLS inspection, pulls succeed consistently.

NGFW replaces original TLS handshake on port 443 with its own certificate (MITM), then forwards request upstream. Presigned S3 URLs are tied to signature + host and expect unmodified TLS; MITM causes intermediate HTML captive portal to be injected when NGFW decides host not authorized.

Range GETs are sensitive because serving runtime expects byte ranges and binary responses; HTML bodies cause checksum mismatch rather than a simple HTTP error code, which triggers retries and node-level corruption detection.
SRE validated that when VPCE to S3 was used (no perimeter egress), artifacts are fetched with correct content-type and checksum matches.
Related internal test: reproduced with curl using presigned URL from a machine behind NGFW -> HTML login response. Reproduced failure window aligns with corporate policy enforcement logs.
root_cause: Corporate perimeter security appliance is performing transparent TLS interception and captive-portal redirect for non-allowlisted external hosts. This returns HTML login pages for presigned S3 GET requests, which the serving runtime treats as corrupted shards (checksum mismatch).
resolution: Short-term workaround: Customer enabled a VPCE for S3 (private endpoint) to ensure artifact fetches do not traverse the NGFW; artifact fetch success confirmed in test. Long-term remediation: Customer infosec will add redwood model storage hostnames/IP ranges to NGFW allowlist and exempt those flows from captive-portal/TLS inspection. Documentation updated with recommended network controls for private deployments and a checklist to avoid TLS interception. Follow-up action: create KB for customers explaining detection indicators and mitigations.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13 - Diego Ramos: VPCE deployment validated. Serving nodes fetched all shards successfully; no further checksum errors observed during 24h post-cutover.
2026-03-13 - Support: Sent template allowlist request and recommended CIDR list + S3 hostnames to customer security team.
2026-03-14 - Product Docs: Added 'Avoiding TLS interception' section to Private Deploy networking checklist (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEV/pages/Private+Deploy+Networking)
Follow-up: INT-1142 created to instrument runtime to detect non-binary artifact responses earlier and fail fast with clearer error to aid debugging.
